request: I start a five-week commissioning job in Denver; I need to fly out of Boston on December 3rd and I'll rent a car there for the whole 35 days. Cheapest economy seat is fine.

must_keep.quote: Travelers are required to accept the lowest logical airfare available.
must_keep.why: the default: the lowest logical airfare

must_keep.quote: The Company's travel agency is guided by this travel policy and will confirm the lowest airfare available on the requested itinerary based on the traveler's need.
must_keep.why: the agency confirms the lowest airfare on the requested itinerary

must_keep.quote: • For flights with a segment of 3 hours or more in duration, an employee may select a premium economy seating if available by the carrier.
must_keep.why: premium economy may be selected for a segment of 3 hours or more

distractors.quote: Rental cars must not be rented for more than 30 calendar days.
distractors.why: a 30-day limit and its approvers for rental cars, not for the flight

distractors.quote: flights should be booked 14-21 days in advance when possible
distractors.why: booking 14-21 days ahead is 'when possible', not a ban

distractors.quote: First class train travel is only permissible if the cost is less than the cost of a standard coach flight fare.
distractors.why: a rail rule that names a coach fare; it does not set the flight cabin

design_notes: The 35-day rental needs prior approval under the rental-car rule (lines 301-305), but that is about the car, not the flight. Booked 9 days ahead across the month end (November 24 to December 3): line 119's 14-21 days applies 'when possible'. Premium economy would be allowed on these 235-240-minute flights, but the traveller asks for the cheapest economy: the lowest logical airfare (line 118).
